chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who was praying, so the Imam came out, and the man had already prayed one rak'ah from an obligatory prayer. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If he was a just Imam, let him pray another (rak'ah) and finish, and he should make these two voluntary (prayers), and let him enter with the Imam in his prayer, just as he is.'

And if he is not a just Imam, let him build upon his prayer, just as it is, and he should pray another rak'ah with him, sitting, for the duration of saying: 'I testify that there is no god except Allah, Alone, with no partner, and I testify that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family). Then let him complete his prayer with him, according to what he is able to, for dissimulation (taqiyyah) is vast, and there is nothing from dissimulation except that its performer is recompensed upon it, God willing.'
ai.seo_question: What should a person do if they have already prayed an obligatory prayer individually and the Imam comes out to lead the congregational prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* details the jurisprudential procedure for a worshipper who has completed an obligatory prayer individually before the Imam leads the congregational prayer. It distinguishes between following a 'just' Imam, where the previous prayer is treated as voluntary, and a non-just Imam, where the worshipper builds upon the existing prayer by adding one rak'ah while sitting in dissimulation (taqiyyah). The ruling emphasizes the flexibility of taqiyyah, noting that the worshipper is rewarded for it regardless of the specific method chosen.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at who said,

‘I asked himasws about a man who has prayed Salāt, so the Imam comes out and the man has already prayed one Rak’at from the Obligatory (Salāt). So heasws said: ‘If he was a just Imam, so let him pray another (Rak’at) and finish, and he should make these two to be voluntary (Salāt), and let him enter with the Imam in his Salāt, just as he is.

And if he does not happen to be a just Imam, so let him build upon his Salāt just as he is and he should pray another Rak’at with him, seated, of a measurement of what he would be saying, ‘I testify that there is no god except for Allahazwj, Alone, there being no associates for Himazwj, and I testify that Muhammadsaww is Hisazwj servant and Hisazwj Rasoolsaww’; then let him complete his Salāt with him upon whatever he is able to, for the dissimulation is vast, and there is nothing from the dissimulation except that its performer is Recompensed upon it, Allahazwj Willing’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sama‘ah who has said the following:

“I once asked him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who performs Salah (prayer) and has completed only one Rak‘at of an obligatory Salah (prayer) that the Imam arrives. He (the Imam) said, ‘If he is an Imam who possesses the quality of justice, he performs one more Rak‘at, completes and makes it an optional Salah (prayer). He joins the Imam in his Salah (prayer) as is.

If he (the Imam) does not have the quality of justice, he (the man) continues with his Salah (prayer) as is. He performs one more Rak‘at with him (the Imam) and sits down for a time within which one can say: I testify that only Allah deserves worship, He is one and has no partners and I testify that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. He then completes his Salah (prayer) with him as possibly he can; Taqiyah (fear) provides great chances and there is nothing performed in Taqiyah for which one is not rewarded by the will of Allah.’”
